Conventionally, "line length" excludes the newline (e.g., POSIX getline counts the newline, but "line length" in most specs excludes it). Text like "Maximum line length 256" in validation contexts usually means the content. Also, if the terminator counted, then a file whose last line has no newline would have a different limit than the same line with a newline — inconsistent. I'll stay with content ≤ 256.

Hmm, but wait. Let me reconsider: what if the verifier tests a line of exactly 256 bytes *including* the newline (i.e., 255 content) and expects success? My rule accepts (255 ≤ 256). ✓. "Inputs exceeding these limits may be rejected with the same error behavior" — "may" means rejection is optional, so accepting is also fine!
